column8: Tue 17 Nov: Table 3 row 6 and 3e: the top-up rides on 7- to 20-year yields, not the Fed's rate; fix bills and the 30-year nothing (the CSV gives the 6-month -1.6%, so say 6-month to 5-year -7.3%); Keel arithmetic, not in NUMBERS.

Tue 17 Nov: for the numbers owner, already open in NUMBERS 9: 5(d) tests DGS1, which carries -0.4% of the ten's rate risk; the report states no odds on most either way, so a register wording point only.
Tue 17 Nov: Table 3 row 6 can name the 10-year as the one yield to watch for the top-up (0.997 over 56 days, CSV tenor_check); Keel arithmetic on FRED repo copies, DGS10 checked at source.

Tue 17 Nov: store or Table 2 note: history on the ten's key rates supports NUMBERS 1's house-model about 8% for a 0.5-point fall before 1 Jan 2027 (9.2% since 1962, 5.2% near today); tails fatter than the model, as the row says.

Tue 17 Nov: 3a or 3e: the $2,388 is a 6 Nov price; 0.357, 1.331 and 3.602 reproduce NUMBERS 4-5, but 0.076, 0.240, 0.547 and 1.087 are not in NUMBERS, so prose uses NUMBERS 5's 0.25-point row ($10,320); keep the words knife edge for 3f's moment.
Tue 17 Nov: claim 1 sized for 3e or Table 3's note; NUMBERS 9 says not a register figure until re-run on the engine; shares of overlapping windows, never odds.
Tue 17 Nov: store variant of row 6 since 1990; 28 of the 35 windows over $38,282 are 2008, so the tail is one episode.
Tue 17 Nov: store variant of row 6 near today's 10-year; the closest sample to carry beside row 6 if history is quoted after registration.
Tue 17 Nov: store robustness check: the $10,000 share holds under the A35 proportional convention, the tail does not (0.38% to 1.8% since 1990).
Tue 17 Nov: three extra days to Mon 4 Jan change little; a footnote to row 6.

Tue 17 Nov: Table 3 row 6 note or 3e, the plainest scale for a judge: these exact weeks cost over $10,000 in 20 of 64 years and over $20,000 in 8 (counts checked against the CSV); register on the engine before use (NUMBERS 9); counts of years, never odds.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e area (2) or Table 3's note: a real dated test of the IPS order (payments whole, floor bought, VT about $1,300 bought, checked in the CSV); $44,993 and $1,318 not in NUMBERS; say a fall the size of 2008's and the largest of these weeks since 1962, never worst on record or the shares fell to; the deposit may shrink too (NUMBERS 5).
Tue 17 Nov: pairs with aha 3: 19 Oct 2023, 8e's one cheap day, was dear ten weeks later; $26,365 and $39,449 not in NUMBERS; say a fall the size of 2023's.
Tue 17 Nov: store context only: the 13 Nov curve is not in NUMBERS (section 9 open, Wed 18 Nov re-run), never today's figure; shows why WORDS dates the $2,388 and the first $38,282.
Tue 17 Nov: store and process on the 13 Nov curve, context until NUMBERS carries it; quote the distance, never the odds, and re-run on the day.
Tue 17 Nov: off-grid twin of NUMBERS 5's own rows (0.5 point: VT $23,458; 1 point: $9,562) and 5(e); prose uses those; never print the floor's written minimum (WORDS).

Tue 17 Nov: 3a or Figure 1's note: checked against NUMBERS 5's grid ($35,894, $34,516, $33,102): the extra Treasuries shrink as yields fall, so the first part of the deposit rises about $259 a basis point, not $314; never called a hedge.

Tue 17 Nov: true on every 56-day window since 1962, but split it: l.13's complete it covers the top-up alone, the extra Treasuries are the reserve's part held as l.11 says, never inside l.13's step; completion for the sum is a register label, not a report word (WORDS).
Tue 17 Nov: store: the order runs and VT takes the move; the clash with most is already in NUMBERS 5(e); never print the written minimum.

Tue 17 Nov: for the lead: a real gap in words, but NUMBERS 0 already puts every carried surplus in the bill ETF, so only a dated line for the first deposit's leftover is missing; the IPS is silent, so Keel's reading.
Tue 17 Nov: 3e area (2) store: in window counts large top-ups are recession events; dense, carry only with row 23's episode count.

Tue 17 Nov: CANON D8 sized, but sixteen-fold is a ratio of overlapping-window shares dominated by 1980-82 and 2008 (row 23: most large episodes had no recession); say far more often, never a multiple.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e area (2): a large top-up does not by itself mean her income is falling; 6 of the 9 episodes without a recession are 1984-87 at 9-14% yields, so cite 1998, 2011 and 2023 for today (checked in the CSV).

Tue 17 Nov: 3e mechanism, but the ten's key rate fell in 7 of 8 recessions (one rise, 1973-75), by under half a point in 5; say that, never mostly did not or mixed; peak to trough misses falls before the peak.
Tue 17 Nov: 3e area (2): a recession brings a sharp eight-week plunge, not a steady slide; 1974 and 2020 only just pass $20,000, and 6.5% of windows without a recession did too.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e area (2) and CANON D8's action: buying the ten in January 2027 takes most rate risk off a year before the deposit her career puts at risk; $7,065 and $57,034 checked against NUMBERS 5 by subtraction; the 2000, 2007 and 2008 figures are MODEL, store only.
Tue 17 Nov: store limit for rows 21-23: NBER lists no peak after Feb 2020, so recent flags are provisional.
Tue 17 Nov: twin of row 31 (the named price lock); Linklaters' definitions kept as its second source.

Tue 17 Nov: the parallel breaks on its own disanalogy: a Balancing Premium settles a data cleanse, not a market move, so never call the top-up one; keep only the risk that the premium moves past what the trustee can afford, beside row 18.
Tue 17 Nov: store: market conditions date names NUMBERS' one-curve convention (6 Nov 2026) against January's price; a paraphrase, so quote only the phrase.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e area (2), one clause at most: the field nearest Laura's plan names the gap between quote and transaction and locks it; Laura cannot (no money until January 2027, no derivatives), so the top-up from her second deposit does that job.
Tue 17 Nov: store: buy-in prices rise as yields fall in every market for fixed payments; textbook bond pricing, the price-chip quote for colour only.
Tue 17 Nov: store answer to why not lock the price first: professionals hold matching bonds before the trade; Laura has no money until January 2027 (case).
Tue 17 Nov: store guard against a year-end rally claim; November starts match all windows.
Tue 17 Nov: Table 3 row 5 support: a fixed first trading day takes the choice of day away, either way; DGS10 read at source; pairs with H1-051 (the 2028 deposit on a fixed date).
Tue 17 Nov: Table 3 form of row 12; Table 3 has no headroom (17 Nov), so a note item at most, once registered.

Tue 17 Nov: for the lead: D8's $1,544 is the curve basis less $300,000 (NUMBERS 1: $301,544); the top-up is $2,287 or $2,388; D8's figure sits in Keel's analysis column, not submitted text, and NUMBERS 9 already lists it.
Tue 17 Nov: store rule restated from SKELETON 3e: shares of overlapping windows, never probabilities.
